preamble: Depalatalization/dentalization of the retroflex nasal [ɳ] to dental-alveolar [n]. In the history of Hindi, Middle Indo-Aryan (Prakrit) -ṇ- and -ṇṇ- surface as n; in modern colloquial Hindi-Urdu, Sanskrit loanword /ɳ/ is usually replaced by /n/; Bengali pronounces ⟨ণ⟩ as [n] except in clusters with retroflex stops. The change is areally concentrated in northern and eastern Indo-Aryan, while Punjabi, Marathi, Gujarati and Odia retain /ɳ/.

examples.note: In casual Hindi and in Urdu, loanword /ɳ/ is usually replaced by /n/ (Ohala 1999)
'quality, virtue'; ⟨ণ⟩ is pronounced [n] outside retroflex clusters
